note: From Shotstack's official pages only. Nothing here was rendered or timed: rendering needs an account (no sign-up was made).

facts.fact: Hosted only: renders run on Shotstack's cloud through its API. No self-hosted or on-premise option found on any official page or in github.com/shotstack (your own AWS can only be a storage destination).
facts.quote: you'll gain a fully managed API, multi-language support, and no infrastructure to maintain

facts.fact: Closed source; Shotstack describes CPU-optimised processing and splitting a video into parts rendered in parallel across servers. GPU is not mentioned. The edit's `instance` field offers s1/s2 and an `a1` 'accelerated instance for faster rendering'.

The render engine and API are proprietary (no engine repository). Open or source-available pieces: SDKs and many demos (MIT), the embeddable Studio editor SDK under the PolyForm Shield License 1.0.0 (source-available, may not be used to compete with Shotstack).

Per rendered minute: pay as you go $10 for 50 min (20¢/min); Starter $39/mo for 250 min (15.6¢); Pro $99/mo for 750 min (13.2¢); Scale $199/mo for 2,000 min (10¢); Volume $499/mo for 10,000 min (5¢). Counted by the second, rounded down. Start free with 10 credits. 4K needs Pro, Scale or Volume (1080p max on pay as you go and Starter).
facts.quote: How are minutes counted? By the second, rounded down. A 30-second video uses half a minute.

facts.fact: Sandbox renders are watermarked, limited to 10 minutes, and need at least one credit on the account.

'Rendering takes approximately 20 seconds per minute of video. Additional effects, filters, or transitions increase render time.' Their 2024 benchmark: a 60 s video at 1080p (1920x1080) in 22.8 s, '3x real time'. Machine and queueing not stated; upload and download time not included. By that rule a 10 s short is about 3-4 s of rendering, but that is their figure, not a measurement here.

Hosted MCP server at https://mcp.shotstack.io/ (Streamable HTTP, OAuth or x-api-key; setup documented for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI); a CLI (@shotstack/cli) with an agent skill; llms.txt; n8n, Make and Zapier integrations.
mp4, gif, mp3, jpg, png, bmp (no webm or mov output). Custom sizes up to 3840 px a side (2160x3840 vertical allowed); fps 12-60 including 30.

facts.topic: what this short needs in Shotstack
facts.fact: Footage, fonts and captions must be at public URLs. Word timings cannot be inlined: rich-caption takes a subtitle file URL (.srt/.vtt/.ttml/.dfxp) or transcribes audio; this edit uses an SRT with one cue per word. Grade: clip `filters` (grade exposure, contrast, saturation). Film grain: no built-in filter; this edit overlays a grain video clip at 12% opacity, which is a workaround, not a documented feature.
